transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... yeah. Um, I came in because... well, for a really long time now, I just wake up already feeling low. It's like there's this heavy, gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic for my shift, and it pretty much just follows me through the whole day. 

I work as a medical assistant, actually, so I'm usually the one rooming people. We just got these new digital thermometers at work last week. They're supposed to be faster, but they keep throwing error codes if the patient moves even a little bit. My supervisor, she gets so mad about it, but it's like, what am I supposed to do, you know? It's kind of like when I was in high school and my dad would get furious if the lawnmower wouldn't start, even though it was completely out of gas and he was the last one to use it... 

Sorry, I lost my train of thought. But yeah, I just always have that heavy feeling on me. Every day.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities you used to like?

I mean... not really? I don't think I've lost interest in stuff. Like, I still play video games when I get home. Usually I play with my buddy Mark from high school. Though he actually just moved to Texas a couple weeks ago because his mom got transferred for her job. They had to drive this massive U-Haul all the way down there, and he was telling me on Discord that the AC went out right when they hit Oklahoma. Can you even imagine? It's been like a hundred degrees out. He said they had to drive with the windows down on the highway the whole time and it sounded like a jet engine in the cab, so they couldn't even hear the radio... 

But, um, what were you asking? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, I don't know, I guess I still like the same things fine. It's just... that heavy feeling is always there while I'm doing them.
Do you often feel tired or like you don't have any energy, even when you haven't done much during the day?

Yeah, all the time. Like, even if I have a day off and sleep in super late, my body just still feels completely worn out. And by the time I finish rooming patients and catching up on all the charts at work... 

Oh man, our charting system is the absolute worst right now. They just updated the software last month, and now every time you try to input the vitals, it makes you click through like three different warning screens. Dr. Miller—he's one of the providers I work with—he actually locked himself out of his account on Tuesday because he forgot his new password and tried guessing it too many times. IT took like four hours to reset it, so we were doing everything on paper. Paper charts! I haven't seen those since I was doing my externship back in high school... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, being tired. Yeah, after work, I get home and I just have absolutely nothing left in the tank. I can't bring myself to do my laundry, or go shoot hoops, or even mess around with my electronics stuff. I'm just totally drained.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

Yeah, actually. It's getting pretty bad. Like, at work, I'll be staring at a patient's intake screen and I just have to reread the same line over and over. And I've caught myself missing little details, like medication doses, or I'll just totally mix up what I was about to ask them next. 

It's kind of like... you know when you're watching a movie and the audio gets out of sync with the video? I was watching this old sci-fi movie the other night, one of the ones from the 80s with the really bad practical effects, and the audio just completely desynced. The guy's mouth was moving, but the sound didn't happen until like two seconds later. It was driving me crazy. I tried pausing it, rewinding it, restarting the app... nothing worked. I ended up just turning it off and staring at the ceiling for like an hour. My ceiling fan has this weird wobble to it, by the way. I keep meaning to tighten the screws, but I never get around to it. 

But yeah, um... my focus is just shot. I can't keep things straight in my head anymore.
Have you felt this way — like there's a heavy, low mood that follows you through the day — for most days over the past couple of years?

Yeah... yeah, it's been a really long time. I'd say most days for about two years and two months now. It all started right around the time the clinic changed up our staffing model and my schedule started rotating all over the place. 

Man, that scheduling system is a nightmare. They brought in this new office manager, Brenda, and she decided we needed to be "more agile" or whatever corporate buzzword she read in a magazine. So one week I'm working four tens, the next week I'm on three twelves, and then suddenly I'm working a weekend shift out of nowhere. Brenda has this weird habit of eating tuna salad at her desk at like 9 AM, too. The whole breakroom area just smells like fish and mayonnaise before I've even had my second cup of coffee. And she uses these really loud mechanical keyboards—clack, clack, clack, all day long. I don't know how she doesn't drive herself crazy. 

Anyway... what was the question? Oh, right, the low mood thing. Yeah, it's been pretty much every day for over two years now, ever since that whole schedule mess started. It just never really lifts.
Before this current period of feeling low, have you ever had any other times in your life when your mood was significantly down for a period of time?

Um, before this? No, not really. Like, high school was mostly fine, I think. I was pretty busy back then anyway, mostly just playing basketball and doing my externship. 

Actually, speaking of basketball, my old coach, Coach Henderson, he just opened up a sporting goods store over on 4th street. I saw a flyer for his grand opening when I was at the grocery store the other day. Which reminds me, that grocery store has been completely out of those jalapeño kettle chips I like for, like, three weeks straight. It's ridiculous. I asked the guy stocking the shelves about it on Sunday, and he just gave me this totally blank stare, like he had no idea what a potato chip even was. And then he dropped a whole box of canned baked beans on the floor. It was a huge mess, dented cans rolling everywhere, and he just stood there staring at them... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Did I feel down before? Uh, no. No, I don't think so. It's really just been this continuous thing for the last couple of years. Before that, I was fine.
